title: Al-Muhsi, the Counter
hook: the Counter, who knows every number
tomorrow: a blank page. what do Muslims say before the first word?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Hamid: praised in every state, even through tears. The line: praised. And a riddle: if His gifts can't be counted, what does the Counter count?

Your phone counts your steps, your screen time, your unread messages. A weekly report shows up on Sunday whether you asked for it or not. Grades, reps, followers, streaks: a lot of the counting in a week is done by things that want something from us. Today's Name is Al-Muhsi, the Counter. And the Qur'an says two things about counting that seem, at first, to collide.
screen: `STEPS, SCREEN TIME, STREAKS.` → `COUNTED ALL WEEK.` → `TWO THINGS THAT COLLIDE.`

segments.voice: The first is in Surah al-Jinn, in Pickthall's words: "He keepeth count of all things." All things. The kindness nobody saw, the shift that ran late, the tear wiped off before anyone noticed. Nothing slips off His tally. The second is in Surah Ibrahim: "if ye would count the bounty of Allah ye cannot reckon it." So there's the answer to yesterday's riddle. The Counter counts everything, every deed and every moment, and the one count we can't finish is His gifts to us. He keeps the full record; our record of what we've been given always comes up short. That changes what counting is for. Counting can be anxious: the reps you missed, the likes that didn't come. Or it can be remembrance. There's a hadith where the Prophet, peace be upon him, told some women among his companions to count their dhikr, their tasbih, on their fingertips, because the fingers will be asked and made to speak. Here's the line to tell a friend tonight: in that hadith, your fingers are witnesses. Counting on them isn't just bookkeeping. It's the body keeping a record of praise.
screen: `HE KEEPETH COUNT OF ALL THINGS.` · `HIS BOUNTY CAN'T BE RECKONED.` · `ANXIOUS COUNTING, OR REMEMBRANCE.` · `FINGERTIPS AS WITNESSES.` · then, large: `COUNTED.`

segments.voice: Hold out one hand. For each finger, name one gift from today, small and specific: a hot shower, a message that came, a door someone held. Then the other hand. When you run out of fingers before you run out of gifts, stop counting, and sit with the leftover.
screen: `ONE GIFT PER FINGER.` · `SIT WITH THE LEFTOVER.`

segments.voice: Al-Muhsi. The Counter: nothing lost from His count, and His gifts beyond ours.
Hold this one: counted, every good thing, by the One whose gifts you'll never finish counting. That's fifteen thirty-one.

howItsDone: Muslims often count dhikr, such as subhanallah, alhamdulillah and allahu akbar after prayer, on their fingers or on prayer beads.

fork.setup: your little cousin counts her dhikr on a phone app. her grandma says, 'use your fingers.' the cousin asks you who's right. what can you honestly tell her?
options: the app; it's more accurate, and Allah counts anyway.
the hadith gives fingers a reason: they'll be asked and made to speak.
neither; counting dhikr at all misses the point of it.
fork.reveal: the Prophet told some companions to count on their fingertips, since fingers will be asked and made to speak. that's a reason grandma can point to; the lesson doesn't call the app wrong.

original.note: Arabic: the Counter, from the traditional list of the Names; the Qur'an speaks of Him keeping count of all things.

trapdoor: what you thought: God as a scorekeeper of sins.
what it means: nothing is lost to Him, good or bad, while His gifts to us outrun our counting.
what a scholar hears: 72:28 'He keepeth count of all things' beside 14:34 'ye cannot reckon it'; fingertips as witnesses (Sunan Abi Dawud 1501).

chat.says: made a chart: pills, reps, ice, steps. dadi looked and said 'you count everything except the good.' rude??
options: Not rude, kind of right. Keep the chart, and add a line for what went well.
Rude. Counting the good is fluffy; the chart is what keeps her safe.
Toss the chart. Allah counts everything, so you don't need to.
chat.meaning: He keeps count of all things, and His gifts can't be counted. Track the care, and still count the good.
